parts: Please review the next brainstorm directions in /shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-2/brainstorm/README.md as well as the recent chat history in investigations-2 for details of how the idea arose. I’ll read the brainstorm agenda and recent research history, then assess the active directions and save a review. If a distinct new direction looks worth pursuing, I’ll add it under `active`.

The 16 folders form a useful menu, but their common bottleneck is finding a theta-specific identity that constrains the physical value and slope. A symmetry of the larger system alone is not enough. I’m checking which proposed first tests could supply that missing information, with parallel reviews of the arithmetic, kernel-sign, and source-preparation approaches.

The review supports a narrower starting group: angular gluing, complete cutoff reflection, and rank-two addition, with source observability as the destination for an identity that survives those tests. A separate lead has also emerged from the collision geometry: a boundary winding calculation may detect collisions inside a time–height region. I’m checking its mathematical scope and whether it adds anything beyond the existing certificates.

I’ll save a repository review using the writing skill and the project’s existing format. The main revision is to rank bounded discovery tests separately from longer-term goals: source observability and kernel factorization are valuable targets, but they still need an independent source identity.

Two concrete findings sharpen the recommendation. A balanced angular coordinate gives an exact heat-compatible theta reflection, but its first angular coefficient vanishes automatically at a collision, so that coefficient adds no exclusion test. Separately, the spacetime calculation gives every finite-multiplicity heat collision a negative local index. This supports a distinct boundary-certificate direction, which I’ll add as a new active folder.

The saved review will recommend three initial identity tests and distinguish supporting tools from longer-term targets. I’ve also prepared `17_spacetime_collision_degree`, including the all-multiplicity argument and exact boundary checks for multiplicities 2–10. Those checks pass; the next step for that direction is to test whether it makes a genuine-theta certificate simpler or cheaper.

Reviewed all 16 directions and the recent chat history. **The portfolio is promising, but I would concentrate the next work on three bounded tests:**

1. **02 Angular Jacobi gluing** — strongest opportunity to use the actual lattice preparation.
2. **01 Complete cutoff reflection** — most direct test of whether reflection improves the complete error bounds.
3. **09 Rank-two addition** — a concrete possible supplier of the paired-kernel signs.

Treat **03 source observability** and **06 kernel factorization** as destinations for successful identities. Keep **08 unit-sector saving** as a separate arithmetic track; the remaining directions merit supporting or tightly capped investigations.

The [full review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-2/brainstorm/reviews/ACTIVE_DIRECTIONS_REVIEW_CODEX_20261013.md) explains each assessment.

I added **[17_spacetime_collision_degree](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-2/active/17_spacetime_collision_degree/README.md)**. Its idea is to exclude interior collisions through a boundary winding calculation. The folder contains an all-multiplicity argument and passing exact polynomial checks; a genuine-theta cost comparison remains the first practical test.

I also saved an [angular refinement](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-2/active/02_angular_jacobi_gluing/notes/ANGULAR_GLUING_AND_RIGIDITY_REVIEW_SEEDS_20261013.md): an exact heat-compatible reflection, together with a demonstration that its first angular coefficient supplies no independent collision constraint.

Navigation is updated. These findings sharpen the research program; they establish no new RH conclusion.
